verses.pali: “Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, appāni ca sulabhāni ca, tāni ca anavajjāni.
verses.english: “Mendicants, these four trifles are easy to find and are blameless.

verses.pali: Paṁsukūlaṁ, bhikkhave, cīvarānaṁ appañca sulabhañca, tañca anavajjaṁ.
Piṇḍiyālopo, bhikkhave, bhojanānaṁ appañca sulabhañca, tañca anavajjaṁ.
Rukkhamūlaṁ, bhikkhave, senāsanānaṁ appañca sulabhañca, tañca anavajjaṁ.
verses.english: Lodgings at the root of a tree …

verses.pali: Pūtimuttaṁ, bhikkhave, bhesajjānaṁ appañca sulabhañca, tañca anavajjaṁ.
Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri appāni ca sulabhāni ca, tāni ca anavajjāni.
verses.english: These four trifles are easy to find and are blameless.

verses.pali: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appena ca tuṭṭho hoti sulabhena ca, idamassāhaṁ aññataraṁ sāmaññaṅganti vadāmīti.
verses.english: When a mendicant is content with trifles that are easy to find, they have one of the factors of the ascetic life, I say.
When you’re content with what’s blameless,
These qualities are said to be
They’re mastered by one who trains,
